highlights.title: All the news about the iPhone Duo
highlights.summary: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo. The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button.
body: The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there. Still, Apple said that preorder demand was “extraordinary,” so it could have a hit on its hands.

The first foldable iPhone is finally here, and following its announcement, we got the chance to try the phone for ourselves. We’ve long been told that Apple would make a foldable iPhone once the tech was good enough — has it been worth the wait?

It definitely feels like something different. The inner screen has a decidedly matte finish that handled even some glare from the windows above the hands-on area well. The folding mechanism is smooth, and even IP68 rated, and the crease is almost impossible to find with my finger. The 5.4-inch outer screen looks petite by modern slab phone standards.
points: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo.
The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease.

highlights.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
highlights.summary: With ia.i, a conversational interface, and the IARA governance platform, Itaú is applying its AI First strategy to customers and employees — in one of Brazil’s most regulated sectors.
body: Creating a close, personalized experience for millions of customers in a country like Brazil is, first and foremost, a question of simplicity rather than of models.
“Much of it is about making something simple, direct, and useful, delivering a direct benefit to the customer, and making the technology almost unnoticeable,” says Carlos Eduardo Mazzei, CTO of Itaú.

The standard he describes is demanding: the solution must solve a real everyday problem and be direct, simple, and memorable. Technology serves as the means, never as the centerpiece of the experience.

There is demand for this. A study by Itaú in partnership with Grupo Consumoteca shows that 80% of Brazilians want to better organize their financial lives and seek more effective support for decisions, and that 65% would like technologies that act as a financial copilot, providing ongoing guidance.

highlights.title: Gloucester claim thrilling draw against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux
highlights.summary: Will Trenholm’s brace was not enough to help Gloucester pull off a stunning upset against Champions Cup holders Bordeaux, as they were forced to settle for a 36-36 draw after a dramatic contest.
body: George Skivington's team pushed the French outfit all the way during a pulsating European tie at Kingsholm Stadium.
Gloucester held a 24-17 lead at half-time before Trenholm crashed over twice, but a double by Louis Bielle-Biarrey salvaged a share of the spoils for visiting Bordeaux.
Bordeaux made a fast start, with Martin Page-Relo able to open the scoring in the fourth minute, but Arthur Clark produced an instant reply for Gloucester.
Efforts by Max Llewellyn and George Barton, either side of Sipili Falatea's try, earned the hosts a slender seven-point advantage at the break thanks to three successful conversions by Barton.

highlights.title: Rockstar Officially Comments on GTA 6's Approach to Trump & COVID-19
highlights.summary: Rockstar Games is known for bringing biting and often puerile satire to its Grand Theft Auto games. The 13-year span between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6 means there's plenty of American culture to interrogate or poke fun at, but a few things will be off the table, according to new…
body: Many GTA players will be happy to hear that, as the games often serve as a fantastical escape that reflects a distorted version of reality. But Rockstar has other reasons for steering clear of real-world historical events.

"We run the risk of dating ourselves in a sort of awkward way," Rockstar North studio head Rob Nelson told The New York Times earlier this summer. "So we have to look at things and go, What is going to have a timeless sort of quality that will speak very easily to relatable sort of human folly and foibles and will be remembered as part of this time?"
It sounds like Rockstar may still make some oblique references to the rise of mainstreaming conspiracy theories in our current culture, an adjacent acknowledgment of Trump and coronavirus.

body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: Apple’s updated App Store rules go after ‘nudify’ AI apps
highlights.summary: Apple's App Store rules now more explicitly ban so-called "nudify" apps that generate intimate images of people without their consent using AI tools. The rule changes follow significant criticism toward Apple after X users used Grok earlier this year to make nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes…
body: As part of updates announced Friday, Apple says that developers “must proactively prevent and remove” nonconsensual, sexual images as part of its content moderation requirements for App Store apps. Developers who “fail to implement adequate safeguards” or “don’t remedy violations after notice” may be removed from the App Store. Apple also clarified a rule that bars “bait-and-switch” apps, or apps that add or change features, including “nudification,” after they have been approved.

Apple’s rules also more clearly spell out that any apps that “facilitate human trafficking or the exploitation of children” will be pulled from the App Store and “blocked from alternative distribution.”

The Italian is 102 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell at the top of the standings, with the first two victories of the year for Red Bull and Max Verstappen only having helped Antonelli move clear of the pack, leaving him with a small chance of being crowned champion in Austin.

Many eyes will be on Antonelli, but Verstappen's quest to complete a hat-trick of wins, along with Lewis Hamilton's attempts to bounce back from a tough Sunday in Singapore promise to provide plenty of entertainment.

highlights.summary: The Red Rising book series by author Pierce Brown has officially been greenlit for a movie adaptation from Paramount Pictures, with Hunger Games alum Francis Lawrence to direct. Red Rising is getting the Hollywood treatment more than a decade after it was first published in 2014.
body: Lawrence is known for his work on another young adult screen adaptation in the Hunger Games series, having directed every movie in the franchise sans the first one, which was directed by Gary Ross. Lawrence recently directed Stephen King adaptation The Long Walk, as well as the forthcoming Sunrise on the Reaping, the latest movie in the Hunger Games franchise.

Lawrence is also set to produce the Red Rising film alongside Cameron MacConomy for their about:blank production company, as well as Francesco Goedhuis and the author of the Red Rising saga himself, Pierce Brown.
Brown reacted to the news in a post on his Instagram account, writing, "Let fall the iron rain. Bloodydamn, I love this team."

Joining Red Rising is Justin Rhodes, who will write the movie’s script. Eagle-eyed IGN readers will recognize this name, as he is also involved in Netflix’s live-action Bioshock movie, which is reportedly still in early development. Rhodes is known for films like Terminator: Dark Fate, Traveler, and Liminal.

highlights.title: The Leap Second Is No More
highlights.summary: The metric might not mean much to laypeople, but leap seconds have been a source of contention in the timekeeping community for years. Now, they’re dead.
body: Leap seconds have driven a raging debate in the metrological community for three decades. Now, that argument has been put to rest: The leap second is officially dead.

Doing away with an obscure metric the average person has been blissfully unaware of may seem like a novelty, but killing the leap second has major ramifications for technology you rely on every day. It also helps stave off what could’ve been a dangerous moment in time: The possibility of the world’s first negative leap second.

The International Bureau of Weights and Measurements (known by its French acronym BIPM) on Thursday said that in May 2027 it would stop issuing leap seconds, 32 of which have been added since 1972 to adjust what’s known as Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

The world implemented the leap second in 1972 due to a growing gap between time measured with atomic clocks and time based on the Earth’s rotation. The reason for the discrepancy? The latter is slowing down due in large part to tidal friction caused by the moon and Earth’s rotation not lining up. The molten core of the Earth as well as oceans and the atmosphere also affect the spin rate.

highlights.title: Fostering community amid Kendall Square’s innovation
highlights.summary: The 18th annual Kendall Square Association Annual Meeting explored how new technologies could be a force for shared prosperity in society.
body: Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is often cited as the most innovative square mile in the world. But when the Kendall Square Association gathered local stakeholders for its 18th Annual Meeting Thursday, the conversation focused on innovation primarily in the context of community.

The event, which took place at the nonprofit startup incubator The Engine, attracted people from across Cambridge, including business leaders, elected officials, local residents, and students, for a night of local food and conversation about the advance of technologies like artificial intelligence and what they mean for society.

“How can we make AI not an enemy of work, but a tool for workers to expand their capabilities and build new expertise or do new things?” asked MIT Institute Professor Daron Acemoglu in a keynote talk. “The world is at a point in time where we need new innovations and new adaptations to growing challenges.”

Acemoglu’s keynote was one of several presentations at the event, which also featured music from the Kendall Square Orchestra, a vote on new KSA board members, and awards for organizations making a positive impact through innovation.

body: Torrential rain on the Thursday resulted in a five-hour delay to the opening round, and there were further frustrations for those still out on the course when play was halted just before 6pm local time on Friday.

McIlroy, who is bidding to win the Race to Dubai title for a record-equalling eighth time, opened the tournament with a two-under 70 on Thursday, while he started his second round with an eagle to sit four under when play was stopped shortly after.

Dutchman Joost Luiten, who had to play 34 holes on Friday because of the delays, Angel Hidalgo and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship winner Adrian Meronk were all able to finish their second rounds, and top the leaderboard on eight under.
Belgian Thomas Detry is also eight under, but is only through six holes of his second round, for which he is currently three under.

highlights.title: James Gunn Shoots Down Milly Alcock Supergirl Rumors, Shares Man of Tomorrow Update
highlights.summary: James Gunn has shot down rumors that Milly Alcock was fired as Supergirl and confirmed that he'll show Peter Safran an early cut of Man of Tomorrow later today. The DC Studios co-chairman took to Threads on October 16 to dispel rumors surrounding his comic book movie projects.
body: First and foremost was the rumor that director Matt Reeves had completely departed The Batman Part 2 as director. Just about everyone now confirmed to be involved in the Elseworlds sequel had already clarified that Reeves would remain involved, so his denial is no surprise here. Another more recent rumor had some fans saying the star of Supergirl was let go, but that one's not true, either.

DC movie watchers feared the worst for Alcock's character after noticing the star had wiped mentions of Kara Zor-El from her Instagram timeline. Although that's not completely true – some photos and Reels related to Supergirl are still very much publicly visible – her standalone film's trouble in theaters had some believing she would be leaving the DCU behind.

Gunn confirmed that's not the case, and it's easy to see why. Alcock first appeared as the character in 2025's Superman and reprised her role in Supergirl when it came out in June. She's been firmly established in the new comic book movie universe, but she's also poised for a triumphant return in Man of Tomorrow.

highlights.title: How Netflix’s Messy Transition Will Rock Hollywood: Looking at You, NBCU
highlights.summary: It started with a dinner. Peter Rice and Ynon Kreiz met for a meal in late September, days before Kreiz surprised the industry by jumping from the CEO job at Mattel to become co-chief executive of Skydance with David Ellison.
body: Media coverage of Kreiz’s courtship of Rice is one of the spurs that pushed Netflix to make the move on a hire that will have ripple effects across its expansive film and TV operations. The ouster of Bela Bajaria from the role that Rice now occupies was messy, and angered many inside and outside of Netflix.

“We don’t live in Hollywood right now. We live in Silicon Valley,” said a prominent agent, citing the general mood of the creative community. The brusque treatment of an executive of Bajaria’s stature is a sign that no one is safe from scrutiny, and no one should ever count on making a graceful exit.

“It feels like more of a tech approach than a studio approach to letting someone go. It’s shameful, it sucks and it adds to the feeling that we’re all working by Silicon Valley rules,” the agent said.

The source noted the irony of Bajaria getting the ax just two weeks after the executive that she replaced at Netflix — Cindy Holland — was also hastily ousted from her new role at Skydance. Holland’s role was sacrificed to make room for Casey Bloys, the HBO chief who is taking over all streaming now that the Warner Bros. Discovery merger is completed.

highlights.title: In a Sprawling Theater Project, 34 Playwrights Make Drama From Democracy
highlights.summary: “It feels like the very pillars of a healthy democracy are under attack,” says Lynn Nottage, one of 30-plus playwrights who have contributed new works to “Women+ on the Edge of Democracy.” “I’m in a moment in my life where every morning when I get up, I think about, ‘What have I done to protect…
body: Heidi Schreck was about to perform her play What the Constitution Means to Me on Broadway one night when her mother called. Apparently, the Tony-nominated work—which examines gender bias in the Constitution through the stories of women in Schreck’s family—had neglected an important figure from history: a hotel maid named Elsie Parrish.

By now, of course, it was a little late; the show had long been locked, and was indeed about to be filmed. But Parrish’s long fight for fairer wages stayed with Schreck—eventually forming the basis for a new play, Searching for Elsie Parrish, which will be published this month in Women+ on the Edge of Democracy.

An anthology of new plays by female-identifying writers, Women+ on the Edge of Democracy was commissioned by the Flynn—a center for performing arts in Burlington, Vermont—in partnership with the Susan Smith Blackburn Prize. It features pieces by playwrights from 30 states who were prompted with two questions: What is the current state of democracy in America? What can history, global context, or futurism offer us in this pivotal moment?

body: The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.

highlights.title: The All Blacks' Haka explained - plus rugby's other rituals
highlights.summary: One of the most intriguing and anticipated moments in the sport of rugby union: the sight of New Zealand's All Blacks performing their world-famous haka as the opposition stands before them.
body: But how much do you know about the haka? And also of the three other ceremonial war dances which take place in rugby: the Cibi, Siva Tau and Sipi Tau.

An ancient traditional Māori practice, there is no single recorded date for the haka's first-ever performance owing to this very reason. It has been practised by indigenous Māori communities for centuries.
The earliest point at which Europeans witnessed the haka was the 18th century: Joseph Banks and James Cook on their first voyage to New Zealand in 1769 recorded the haka as "vigorous and ferocious".

In terms of its introduction into sport, New Zealand's first rugby union side visited Australia in Sydney in 1884 and performed the haka. During 1888/89, a 'New Zealand native team' toured the UK for the first time, performing the haka on October 3 1888 against Surrey in a tour match.

highlights.title: 8 Call of Duty Games Still Missing from Game Pass
highlights.summary: The franchise has slipped from its lofty perch in recent years, but there was a time when the launch of a new Call of Duty game was a huge event. The anticipation was never quite on the level of Grand Theft Auto 6, but the series reliably mattered in a way that many other games did not.
body: When Microsoft purchased Activision, some of us assumed we wouldn’t have to wait long before being able to play all of those classic games on Xbox Game Pass. Why else would Microsoft drop that kind of money on the company, if not to leverage its library of classics? But Call of Duty has made only a weak showing on the subscription service since then, with many of its most iconic games still available only for purchase. With Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launching Oct. 23, here are eight Call of Duty games somehow still missing from Game Pass. We’d love to see them get added soon.

After Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, it was unclear how the franchise might top itself. Then came Call of Duty: Black Ops, with an energetic campaign that included outrageous moments such as an attempted assassination of Fidel Castro. Some of the most memorable characters in the franchise experienced a thrilling campaign, and that was just for starters. Without Black Ops, we never would have been introduced to the Nuketown map so many of us know and love from multiplayer deathmatch. The game’s absence from Game Pass is an injustice.

The scrum-half Olivia Apps said in the buildup to these matches that Canada had been doing everything they can in 2026 to make it possible to beat England and that is just what they did.

It was Apps who was one of Canada’s standout players in a cold Toronto with Sophie de Goede her usual best and the player of the match DaLeaka Menin a hugely valuable asset. highlights.summary: Supercell has confirmed Squad Busters will be removed from the App Store and Google Play on December 1 and stop being playable on December 14. The developer said players who already have the game installed can keep playing until December 14, with all events and timers ending on that date.
body: Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026. In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
The developer said it could not see “a clear path forward” for the game after several reworks, including its Heroes update. It said further changes would have made it almost a completely new game.

Squad Busters launched worldwide in May 2024. AppMagic estimates put its lifetime revenue at about $67.9m from 58.6m downloads, with the US accounting for 30% of spending. That works out at an estimated $1.16 in revenue per download globally.
The company has also ruled out offline play, private servers and releasing the code, saying the game contains content and characters from across its other titles.

body: Video shows the crash that injured two CHP officers responding to an earlier incident on I-80.

Video released by CHP shows the Tesla speeding past flares, cones, and emergency lights where officers were on the scene of an earlier accident, before ramming into the back of a parked patrol vehicle. CHP says two officers were seriously injured in the accident and taken to a hospital.

Following numerous collisions with parked emergency vehicles, NHTSA launched an investigation into Tesla’s Autopilot software in 2021. It eventually issued a report finding the driver-assist features didn’t do enough to keep drivers engaged, linking them to hundreds of crashes and dozens of deaths when both the system and driver failed to respond.

Tesla released an update for Autopilot in 2023 adding more controls and alerts to prompt drivers to be in full control of the car when Autosteer is enabled, but NHTSA then had to open another investigation into whether those changes went far enough.

highlights.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn’t Get to Say ‘I’ or ‘Me’
highlights.summary: MIT professor Sherry Turkle warns that people have become dangerously enmeshed with chatbots.
body: During four decades of studying the effects of interaction with computers, Sherry Turkle has developed a reputation as a careful if critical social scientist who approaches her work with academic rigor and distance.

Her new book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, breaks this mold. It is a polemic warning that we have reached a state of emergency where our humanity is at risk from overreliance on soulless machines who pose as our tutors, mentors, friends, colleagues, and lovers. Turkle is aiming for the high bar of books — Silent Spring, The Jungle, Unsafe at Any Speed —that awaken the public to impending crises.
Essentially, this diminutive MIT professor is taking on a multitrillion-dollar industry backed by a government eager to accelerate AI into every corner of our personal and professional lives.

STEVEN LEVY: Your previous books reported results of your research as a social scientist, often leading to troubling conclusions about how people, especially children, interact with computers. But this book reads like you’re breaking the glass and pulling the fire alarm. Why the shift?

highlights.title: Street Fighter: How Can There Be an Ending Explained When There Is No Ending?
highlights.summary: Street Fighter is in theaters now, so this is our ending explained... or rather, non-ending explained. Plus, are there any post-credits scenes in the new movie?
body: Let's make this simple: You want to know if there are any mid- or post-credits scenes in Street Fighter. The answer is yes, as the film features an animated mid-credit scene.

Street Fighter is back on the big screen this week, with the third live-action incarnation of the popular video game franchise after attempts in 1994 and 2009. Was the third time the charm? Well, as Tom Jorgensen’s Street Fighter review for IGN notes, not exactly, though it’s certainly superior to The Legend of Chun-Li.

So how did things play out in this go-around? The story this time centers on old friends Ken (Noah Centineo) and Ryu (Andrew Koji), who are reunited after a years-long rift when they are both recruited by Chun-Li (Callina Liang) for the second-ever World Warrior tournament, which is being presented by Shadaloo dictator M. Bison (David Dastmalchian).

Soon, the best fighters in the world are gathering in Shadaloo, even as Bison has ulterior motives for holding the tournament at all, as his main goal is to get ahold of Ryu – the winner of the one previous World Warrior – in order to drain his “Hado Power” (which gives Ryu the rare ability to create a Hadouken) for himself.
